page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.6xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented instance belonging to the High Clock Speed ecs.hfg5 family. Built on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine provides 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. System memory totals 96.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware resource provisions omit dedicated physical graphics hardware and local disk storage. Because bundled storage is rated at None, instances rely entirely on attached network block storage volumes for system and runtime data. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

The 3.1 GHz base clock speed delivers robust per-thread compute density, making this instance suitable for workloads constrained by processing frequency. From an infrastructure cost efficiency perspective, allocating high-clock dedicated cores alongside a 1:4 memory footprint maximizes compute-heavy throughput without paying for unused memory tiers or idle local drive arrays. Operating tradeoffs include dependency on remote network storage for disk I/O and baseline network bandwidth limited to 4 Gbps.

The ecs.hfg5.6xlarge instance fits CPU-bound enterprise applications, high-throughput web serving tiers, continuous integration build clusters, and middle-tier transactional database services where consistent single-thread processor frequency is required.
